data.cultural_impact: The name "Yeswanth" originates from Indian culture, specifically from the Hindu faith. It is a beautiful sounding name that carries a deep meaning and connection to the Hindu deity, Lord Shiva. In Hindu culture, names are not just given arbitrarily but are chosen based on various factors such as religious significance, family history, and astrological influences. The name "Yeswanth" is a perfect reflection of the deep devotion and connection that many Hindus have towards Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Yeswanth" signifies a person who embodies the qualities of Lord Shiva, such as joy, love, and devotion. In Hinduism, Lord Shiva is considered to be the supreme God of destruction and transformation. He is also known as the god of love and marriage. The name "Yeswanth" is a reminder of the spiritual ideal of being fully devoted to the divine and experiencing the joy and love that comes with it. It is a powerful reminder of the importance of staying connected to the divine and living a life of love, compassion, and devotion towards Lord Shiva.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Yeswanth is a name derived from the Sanskrit word 'Yashas' meaning fame or glory, and 'Vantha' meaning desiring or longing. Together, Yeswanth symbolizes one who longs for or desires fame and glory.

historical_references.reference: Yeswanth, also known as Vibhishana, was the younger brother of King Ravana in Hindu mythology. He is considered a loyalist and an advisor to Ravana, and is also referred to as the 'King of Lanka'. He is described as a just and virtuous being who ultimately took the side of Rama in the epic battle between Rama and Ravana for the abducted Sita.

Yeshantha was a celebrated military general under the Chalukya king Kirtivarma I (ruled 597-623 AD) in early medieval India. He is known for his victories in several battles, including the one against the Pallava king Mahendra Varman I (ruled 600-630 AD).
